title: How far does the tortoise walk in half an hour?
description: The tortoise walks one quarter of a kilometre in one hour, and the video finds the distance for half an hour by cutting the shaded quarter of a unit square into two equal parts. Keeko then raises a hand with the doubt that the tops and the bottoms can be added.
teaching_notes: One idea: a fraction of a fraction means cutting the part again into equal parts, so the whole ends up in more, smaller parts. Watch for students who add the tops and add the bottoms.

source: {{NAME_1}}'s pet tortoise walks 1/4 km in 1 hour. How far can it walk in half an hour?
video_script.why: The child can take a fraction of a whole number and now meets a fraction of a fraction, which a unit square shows by cutting a part again.
video_script.substitution: Half of one quarter is one of the two equal parts we get when one quarter is cut into two, and the whole then has eight equal parts.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_1}}'s pet tortoise walks one quarter of a kilometre in one hour: how far in half an hour?
video_script.wrong_move: adds the two tops and the two bottoms of one half and one quarter and gets two sixths, which is more than one quarter
video_script.payoff_line: The tortoise walks one eighth of a kilometre in half an hour
video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one quarter, one eighth, two sixths

names.{{NAME_1}}: walks 3 km in 1 hour; his pet tortoise walks 1/4 km in 1 hour

maths_rules: the quarter cut into 2 equal parts makes the whole 4 × 2 = 8 equal parts, with 1 shaded
the slip: 2/6 = 1/3, which is more than 1/4
video_script.design: One idea: half of a quarter means cutting the shaded quarter into two equal parts. The unit square is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

<bookmark mark='walk'/>The tortoise walks one quarter of a kilometre in one hour.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How far can the tortoise walk in half an hour?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='square'/>Draw a square and take it as the whole.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>We can cut the whole into equal parts.

marks.given: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the tortoise walks one quarter of a kilometre in one hour.

beats.on_screen: To find: distance in half an hour

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the distance the tortoise walks in half an hour.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Step one, write the distance as a multiplication.
Half an hour is one half of an hour.
We take one half of one quarter of a kilometre.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the unit square is the whole; the square is cut into 4 equal parts and 1/4 of it is shaded

marks.whole: the unit square is taken as the whole
marks.shade: one quarter of the square is shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Step two, take the unit square as the whole.
<bookmark mark='shade'/>Cut it into four equal parts and shade one quarter.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the shaded quarter is cut into 2 equal parts; the whole now has 4 × 2 = 8 equal parts, and 1 part is shaded

marks.cut: the shaded quarter is cut into two equal parts
marks.eight: the whole now shows eight equal parts
marks.one: one of the eight parts stays shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step three, cut the shaded quarter into two equal parts.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>The whole is now cut into eight equal parts.
<bookmark mark='one'/>One of these parts is shaded.

marks.pay: the answer stays on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>One part out of eight is one eighth, so one half times one quarter is one eighth.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The tortoise walks one eighth of a kilometre in half an hour.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 1/2 × 1/4 = 2/6 is written and crossed out; 2/6 is drawn longer than the shaded quarter; the unit square with 8 parts is shown again

marks.fix: 2/6 is drawn longer than the shaded quarter and the line is crossed out
marks.rule: the shaded quarter is cut again into two equal parts

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is two sixths of a kilometre.
Keeko added the tops and added the bottoms.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But two sixths is more than one quarter.
Half an hour cannot take the tortoise further than a whole hour.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>A part of a part is smaller than the part. We cut the part again into equal parts.
